Home
Learning and Growing Together in the Light of God's Love
Welcome to St Joseph's, Dorking
At St Joseph’s Catholic Primary school, we believe every child is unique, valued, and capable of achieving great things. Our school is a vibrant, caring community where children are encouraged to grow in confidence, curiosity, and kindness. We are proud of our strong sense of family, our commitment to high standards, and the joyful atmosphere that makes learning here so special.
Want to know more? Explore our website to discover what makes St Joseph’s such a special place. Don’t forget to visit our Latest News section, where you’ll find updates on school life, achievements, and upcoming events. It’s the best way to see our school community in action!

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Joseph's Catholic Primary School - Dorking Schools' Partnership
pageCache.text:
Dorking Schools' Partnership
The Dorking Partnership aims to create an effective network, maximising the educational opportunities for the local community.
We are a group of fifteen local schools, who work together to provide the children and families in Dorking and the surrounding villages with a range of opportunities and support.
By working together as schools and collaborating with others within our local community we seek to raise achievement and aspiration. For example, through procuring specialist services, ensuring cohesion between professional agencies, providing parenting support, sharing expertise and resources, and providing a range of out-of-school and sporting activities for the benefit of our pupils, their families, our staff and members of the wider community.

We got the silver!

We are incredibly proud of their achievement and the way they demonstrated commitment and resilience from start to finish.

Inspection Reports
Inspection Reports
We are delighted to publish our most recent Catholic School Inspection, where we were graded as 'Outstanding' in all three areas and outstanding in all 9 sub-categories.
Our Ofsted Inspection in March 2023 confirmed St. Joseph’s as a "Good" school; we are proud of this achievement.
In June 2019, our school was graded as "Outstanding" in all areas by the Diocesan inspectors in our Section 48 Ofsted Inspection; retaining our previous "Outstanding" grading form 2014.. We are delighted with this commendation of the work we do as a Catholic school.
Both reports can be accessed below for you to read in full or may be viewed on the Ofsted website and the Diocesan website.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Joseph's Catholic Primary School - Pastoral Care
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care
We are proud of our high level of pastoral care. We make great efforts to ensure that every child feels happy and safe at St. Joseph’s as we believe this is when they will learn best. Standards of behaviour are consistently high and children learn the importance of respecting everyone. We recognise that everyone sometimes makes mistakes, but when this happens a strong emphasis on forgiveness and reconciliation allows us to move forward and genuinely learn from these mistakes. Older children are expected to act as role models and have opportunities to support and care for younger ones, for example through our House system and Playground Pals. We are committed to meeting the individual learning needs of each child in our school, continually developing our approaches to teaching. We seek to develop children in all areas- academic, personal, social, emotional and spiritual.
Teaching assistants provide extra support within every classroom and also work with children one-to-one or in small groups outside the classroom when appropriate.
We have a teaching assistant who is specially trained to provide support in Emotional Literacy and we also employ a Home School Liaison Worker who supports families on a wide range of issues.
Our parish priests have always supported the work of the school, for example, visiting the school regularly, visiting classrooms and providing pastoral support for pupils, families and staff. The headteacher is a member of the Parish Pastoral Group.

Curriculum
You can find our curriculum information using the links in the sidebar.
If you have any questions about our school curriculum, please contact the school office via email on:
office@stjosephs-dorking.surrey.sch.uk
Our Early Years Curriculum
The curriculum that we deliver in the Year R (Reception) class meets the requirements set out in the Government’s Curriculum Guidance for the Foundation Stage. This sets out the standards that must be met to ensure that children learn and develop well and are healthy and safe. Children develop skills, acquire new knowledge and demonstrate their understanding through seven areas of learning and development. These areas are divided into the ‘Prime’ and ‘Specific’ areas of learning.
The three ‘Prime’ areas of learning focus on developing the skills that children need for healthy development and to become effective learners. These areas are:
As children grow, the Prime areas will help them to develop skills in four ‘Specific’ areas, which are:
These seven areas are used to plan children’s learning and activities. It is designed to be flexible so that staff can follow the needs and interests of the children. Children in the EYFS learn through playing and exploring, being active, and through creative and critical thinking which takes place both indoors and outside.
Each child’s progress is reviewed throughout the year through on-going assessment against the early learning goals. The assessment is based on classroom observation and children do not sit tests. It uses the early learning goals, which can be found in the Early Years Framework which can be accessed here

Physical Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the world

Our Curriculum at Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2
Mathematics: We follow the National Curriculum for Maths, placing emphasis on core skills to ensure that an understanding of place value, addition, subtraction, multiplication and division are embedded from an early age. Teachers' plan lessons to include a balance of opportunities to develop fluency, reasoning and problem-solving. Teachers have been trained in the Mastery Approach and have been involved in Teacher Research Groups in this area.
English: We follow the National Curriculum for English, focusing on the key skills of phonics, reading and spelling; grammar, punctuation and writing; and speaking and listening. We use "Unlocking Letters and Sounds", a DfE validated Synthetics Phonics Programme, to teach phonics. Children in Yrs R – 2 have a daily phonics session. We promote a 'phonics first' approach and in both our guided reading sessions at school and in the books children take home, texts are very closely matched to a child's current phonics knowledge so that every child can experience real success in their reading. In these crucial early stages of reading we primarily use books from Ransom Reading Stars Phonics. As well as their reading scheme book, children are encouraged to choose books from our class book corners and school library to encourage reading for pleasure. Once children progress beyond decodable texts, they move onto our book scheme so that they can continue to progress in their decoding, fluency and comprehension skills to become avid, expert readers.
Science: Our science curriculum follows the National Curriculum, organised through topics each term for each year group.
Religious Education: As a Catholic School, we devote 10% of curriculum time to the teaching of Religious Education; this is separate from times of prayer and collective worship, such as assemblies, liturgies and class prayer which happen in addition to the taught curriculum.
At St Joseph's we follow the Religious Education Directory (RED) Model Curriculum in ‘To know you more clearly – June 2023’. The RED fulfils the requirements of the Bishop's Conference which sets forth the expectations for what should be covered by Religious Education teaching in Catholic Schools in England and Wales.
The RED is a transformative Religious Education programme designed to deepen students’ spiritual growth by nurturing a rich understanding of Catholic beliefs and values.
PHSE and RSE: We follow a programme which is recommended by the Diocese of Arundel and Brighton known as Ten Ten: Life to the Full.
We follow the National Curriculum requirements for Art and Design, Computing, Design Technology, Geography, History, Music and Physical Education.
Our teachers have created a Topic Framework which seeks to provide a broad and balanced curriculum, draws links between areas of learning and includes an exciting range of challenging tasks designed to help children think independently and work creatively.
Sometimes subjects and skills are taught in discrete lessons, at other times subjects may be grouped together in topics. For example, a topic may have a History focus such as the Ancient Egyptians but children may also use geographical skills to interpret maps, learn about the importance of the River Nile or study Egyptian art.
We also place emphasis on the skills needed to become effective learners. We promote a “Growth Mindset”, for example encouraging children to take risks in their learning and challenge themselves, valuing mistakes as learning opportunities, building resilience and perseverance and valuing the learning process as well as the outcomes.
PE: In addition to PE and Games lessons, each year group has a block of swimming lessons during the year. EYFS and KS1 have their lessons at Dorking Leisure Centre and KS2 have their lessons at the Priory School Pool with Swimsense. We are an active member of the Dorking Schools’ Sports Partnership and participate in a wide range of local festivals, competitions and tournaments.
Languages: We teach French as our modern foreign language to children from Year 1 - 6.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Joseph's Catholic Primary School - World Earth Day!
pageCache.text:
World Earth Day!
Join us in being stewards of our common home!
Our school marked World Earth Day with a wonderful sense of community and care for our common home. Several classes joined a national live lesson, exploring ways we can protect and cherish the environment. Across the school, pupils took part in special activities that encouraged reflection, creativity, and action. We also gathered for a thoughtful liturgy inspired by Laudato Si’, Pope Francis’ letter reminding us of our shared responsibility to look after the Earth. It was a meaningful day that helped us deepen our commitment to caring for creation.

pageCache.text:
Epsom & Redhill Deanery
We have a long and successful history of collaboration with the other Catholic schools in the Epsom and Redhill Deanery and are proud to be an active, strategic partner in this group of schools.
We work together for the benefit of the children in our schools, providing school-to-school support and sharing expertise and resources. Key areas of collaboration are professional learning and development for our staff and supporting initial teacher training.
Initial Teaching Training .
We place student teachers in our local Catholic schools and assist them towards becoming excellent practitioners. We have links with Xavier Teaching Hub, St. Mary's Twickenham and Roehampton.
Admissions to St Andrew's and oversubscribed Catholic schools
Please see the document below for information about the 'Certificate of Catholic Practice' (CCP) which is being implemented for admissions to oversubscribed Catholic Schools.
This will be in place for admissions from September 2027, and will apply to all families applying to St Andrew's.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Joseph's Catholic Primary School - Jubilee 2025 - Pilgrims of Hope
pageCache.text:
Jubilee 2025 - Pilgrims of Hope
Pope Francis decided that 2025 would be a year of Jubilee, something which happens every 25 years. The theme is "Pilgrims of Hope". The Pope invited Catholics to renew our hope and discover a vision that can "restore access to the fruits of the earth to everyone". We are also invited to rediscover a spirituality of God's creation in which we understand ourselves as "pilgrims on the earth" rather than masters of the world.

Meet Julio: Our Jubilee Bear
Julio, our Jubilee bear, has joined the children in some liturgies, lessons and clubs.
Jubilee Launch Day 2025
The children took part in the schools’ launch of the Jubilee Year today. Pope Francis has chosen the theme of ‘Pilgrims of Hope’. The Year 6 members of the Lily Squad lead us in our launch liturgy. The children have also been involved in class-based activities, thinking about the meaning behind the logo and also finding out more about the theme of hope and how they can be signs of hope in the world by putting Catholic Social Teaching into action. We look forward to journeying through the year ahead.

Our School Pledge Day
We held our own school 'Pledge Day' where each class thought about what pledges they would like to make. Children thought about our Catholic Social Teaching Principles and how they would consider these when making their pledges. Class representatives showed the rest of the school a selection of their pledges at a special assembly. We joined all of our pledges together to make our St Joseph's Jubilee pledge, which is linked at the bottom of this page.
Good Shepherd Celebration
Every year, all the schools in our Diocese are invited to send representatives to participate in the Good Shepherd Celebration, a special service organised by the Diocesan Education Service and celebrated by Bishop Richard Moth. This year, to mark the Jubilee, the service took place at Arundel Cathedral and each school presented their pledges for the Year of Hope. Representatives from St Joseph's presented Bishop Richard with a Pilgrims of Hope dove which was holding our St Joseph's School pledge.
